claim: Definition of the Wasserstein-1 distance between two probability measures as the infimum of the expected transport cost over all couplings.
Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality: the Wasserstein-1 distance equals the supremum of the difference of expectations over all 1-Lipschitz test functions.
Definition of the Lipschitz seminorm of a real-valued function as the supremum over distinct points of the ratio of the function increment to the distance.
Definition of the operator Lipschitz seminorm for matrix-valued functions, using the operator norm of the matrix increments.
Definition of Ollivier (coarse) curvature at time t for a time-inhomogeneous Markov chain: one minus the worst-case ratio of one-step Wasserstein distance to the original distance.
Positive Ollivier curvature implies the Markov averaging operator contracts the Lipschitz seminorm by a factor of (1-kappa_t).
Positive-curvature-on-average assumption: the effective curvature kappa bounds the sum of products of per-step contraction factors for every time horizon.

Main Chernoff bound in the curvature regime: a sub-Gaussian tail for the largest eigenvalue of a sum of centered matrix observables of a positively curved inhomogeneous chain, with variance proxy of order L^2 D^2 / kappa.
Oscillation chain bound: each observable has positive oscillation bounded by the maximal oscillation Delta_op, which is at most L times D.
Definition of Delta_op as the largest operator-norm oscillation of the observables across all times.
Uniform curvature assumption: every time step of the chain has Ollivier curvature at least kappa > 0.
Improved Chernoff bound with logarithmic diameter dependence: under uniform curvature and bounded oscillation the variance proxy drops to order Delta_op^2 kappa^{-1} (1 + log(LD/Delta_op)).

Elo rating update rule: after a match between players I and J, the winner's rating moves up and the loser's moves down by eta times the sigmoid of the rating gap, and ratings not involved are unchanged.
Definition of the environment metric d_E combining the Euclidean distance of true ratings with the total-variation distance of matchup distributions.
Definition of total-variation distance between two matchup distributions over unordered player pairs.
Definition of the joint metric d_Z on Elo ratings plus environment as the sum of the rating distance and the environment distance.
equation: d_{\mathcal Z}\bigl((x,e),(\widetilde x,\widetilde e)\bigr) \coloneqq \|x-\widetilde x\|_2+d_{\mathcal E}(e,\widetilde e).

claim: Markov transition structure of the environment process: the next environment is drawn from the kernel Gamma_t given the current environment.
Definition of the filtration F_t capturing all environment, rating, matchup, and outcome information available just before match t.
Conditional matchup selection: given the history, the pair playing match t is drawn from the current matchup distribution q^t.
Logistic (Bradley-Terry) win model: the conditional probability that player I beats player J is the sigmoid of their true-rating gap.
Factorization of the joint Elo-environment transition kernel into the environment kernel Gamma_t and the fixed-environment Elo kernel K_{e'}.
equation: P_t\bigl((x,e),d x' d e'\bigr) =\Gamma_t(e,d e')\,K_{e'}(x,d x').

claim: Definition of lambda(e), the algebraic connectivity (second-smallest Laplacian eigenvalue) of the matchup graph, measuring how fast match information propagates between players.
Uniform lower bound assumption on the matchup graph's algebraic connectivity across all environments.
Definition of kappa, an explicit lower bound on Elo's one-step curvature when the environment is fixed, proportional to the step size, e^{-4M}, and the connectivity lambda.
Contraction assumption on the environment chain: it has one-step Wasserstein curvature at least nu under the environment metric.
equation: W_1^{d_{\mathcal E}}\bigl(\Gamma_t(e,\cdot),\Gamma_t(\widetilde e,\cdot)\bigr) \le (1-\nu)d_{\mathcal E}(e,\widetilde e) \qquad \text{for all }t\ge1\text{ and }e,\widetilde e\in\mathcal E.

claim: Step-size constraint for the Elo analysis: the update step eta is at most half of the environment curvature nu.
Fixed-environment curvature lemma: one step of Elo contracts the Wasserstein distance between rating distributions by a factor of (1-kappa).
Environment-sensitivity lemma: changing the environment perturbs one Elo step by at most eta times the environment distance.
Lipschitz bound for the logistic win probability: the sigmoid is 1/4-Lipschitz, so win-probability differences are controlled by rating-gap differences.
Augmented curvature lemma: the joint Elo-plus-environment chain contracts in Wasserstein distance by (1-kappa) under the joint metric.
Optimal-coupling identity: the expected environment distance under the optimal coupling equals the Wasserstein distance, which contracts by (1-nu).
equation: \E d_{\mathcal E}(E',\widetilde E') = W_1^{d_{\mathcal E}}\bigl(\Gamma_t(e,\cdot), \Gamma_t(\widetilde e,\cdot)\bigr) \le (1-\nu)d_{\mathcal E}(e,\widetilde e).

claim: Conditional coupling bound for the joint chain: the expected rating distance contracts by (1-kappa) plus an eta-weighted environment term.
equation: \E\!\left[ \|X'-\widetilde X'\|_2 \middle| E',\widetilde E' \right] \le (1-\kappa)\|x-\widetilde x\|_2 +\eta d_{\mathcal E}(E',\widetilde E').

claim: Combined one-step bound for the joint chain, summing the environment and rating contributions before the parameter algebra is simplified.
equation: W_1^{d_{\mathcal Z}}\bigl(P_t(z,\cdot),P_t(\widetilde z,\cdot)\bigr) \le (1-\kappa)\|x-\widetilde x\|_2 +(1+\eta)(1-\nu)d_{\mathcal E}(e,\widetilde e).

claim: Drift assumption: the expected one-step change of the true ratings, measured by a squared l2 term plus an l1 cross term, is bounded by Delta.
Elo tracking lemma: the expected squared distance of Elo ratings to the moving true ratings decays geometrically from initialization plus steady-state drift and noise terms.
One-step conditional contraction of Elo's squared tracking error for a fixed environment.
Cross-term bound controlling the inner product of the tracking error with the rating drift by the l1 drift.
Squared-norm expansion splitting the tracking error into the previous error, the drift increment, and their cross term.
One-step recursion for the expected squared tracking error, adding the drift term Delta to the contraction.
Granularity assumption: the environment's one-step support has bounded diameter in true ratings (h_rho) and in matchup distributions (h_q).
Bound on the one-step support diameter of the augmented chain in the joint metric: 2*sqrt(2)*eta + 2*h_rho + 4*sqrt(2)*h_q.
Burn-in time condition for the pointwise Elo tracking theorem, scaling as kappa^{-1} log(nM/(epsilon eta)).
Pointwise Elo tracking theorem: after burn-in, the distance of Elo ratings to true ratings exceeds the bias-plus-fluctuation level with probability at most 2e^{-epsilon^2}.
Definition of the scalar observable f(x,rho,q) = ||x-rho||_2 used to apply concentration to Elo tracking; it is 1-Lipschitz in the joint metric.
Concentration of the tracking observable around its mean, with a sub-Gaussian rate governed by the curvature kappa and the granularity B.
Optimal step-size scaling conclusion: ignoring granularity terms, the tracking bound is minimized by choosing the step size eta of order sqrt(Delta).
Averaging-window condition for the averaged-Elo theorem, scaling as epsilon^{-2} eta^{-2} M^2 n log(n/delta).
Averaged Elo theorem: time-averaged Elo ratings concentrate around time-averaged true ratings with high probability.
Pointwise bias bound: the expected tracking error at time k decays geometrically from initialization plus steady-state drift and noise floors.
Geometric-series bound used to average out the initialization term over the averaging window.
Averaged bias bound: the expected averaged tracking error is bounded by drift and noise terms plus a vanishing initialization term.
Matrix dilation embedding the tracking-error vector into a Hermitian block matrix so the matrix Chernoff bound applies.
Matrix concentration for the averaged tracking error, with dimension factor (n+1)^{2-pi/4} and rate governed by kappa and the diameter.
Informal main result of the paper: a sub-Gaussian tail bound for the largest eigenvalue of summed centered matrix observables of an inhomogeneous positively-curved chain.
Improved variance-proxy order Delta_op^2 kappa^{-1} (1 + log(LD/Delta_op)) achieved under bounded oscillation, replacing the diameter factor.
Optimality remark: without an oscillation bound, the variance proxy L^2 D^2 kappa^{-1} is optimal up to constants.
Comparison bound from related work: a variance proxy of order L^2 sigma_infty^2 kappa^{-2}, which is worse whenever mixing is much slower than the chain's granularity.
Definition of the chain granularity sigma_infty as the supremum over time and state of the one-step support diameter.
Tropp one-step lemma: the Markov operator applied to a trace-exponential of a centered matrix function is bounded by a trace-exponential with a variance correction 2A^2.
Definition of the local granularity sigma_infty(x) as the diameter of the one-step transition support from state x.
Induction lemma: the trace-exponential moment generating function contracts with an added 2 L^2 sigma_infty^2(x) identity term; the key building block of the mgf argument.
Operator-norm deviation bound: on the one-step support, an L-Lipschitz matrix function deviates from its mean by at most L times the local granularity.
Definition of the global granularity sigma_infty as the supremum of one-step support diameters over all times and states.
Single-observable concentration theorem: an L-Lipschitz matrix observable at time T concentrates around its mean with sub-Gaussian rate kappa/(L^2 sigma_infty^2).
Iterated mgf bound: after iterating the induction lemma, the matrix moment generating function is controlled by the mean plus a curvature-discounted variance sum.
Geometric-series bound: the curvature-discounted sum of squared contraction products is at most kappa^{-1} under the effective-curvature assumption.
Alternative effective-curvature assumption for the empirical-mean theorem, with a shifted summation range and effective curvature tilde-kappa.

Matrix MCMC theorem: the empirical mean of L-Lipschitz matrix observables concentrates with rate tilde-kappa^2 T/(L^2 sigma_infty^2), at the cost of a quadratic kappa dependence and no diameter bound.
Lipschitz bound on the auxiliary function g in the induction step, controlled by the effective curvature tilde-kappa.
Final mgf bound for the empirical mean of matrix observables, with variance term 2 s^2 L^2 sigma_infty^2/(tilde-kappa^2 T).
equation: \E_{X_0}\!\left[\tr\exp\left(\frac{s}{T} \sum_{k=1}^T F_k(X_k)\right)\right] &\le \tr\exp\left(\frac{s}{T} \sum_{k=1}^T P_{1} \cdots P_{k} F_k(X_0) + \frac{2 s^2 L^2 \sigma_\infty^2}{\tilde\kappa^2T} \Id \right) \\ &= \tr\exp\left(\E_{X_0}\!\left[\frac{s}{T} \sum_{k=1}^T F_k(X_k)\right] + \frac{2 s^2 L^2 \sigma_\infty^2}{\tilde\kappa^2T} \Id \right).

claim: Definition of the time-inhomogeneous Markov transition: the conditional law of X_t given X_{t-1} = x is P_t(x, .).
The time-t marginal distribution equals the initial distribution pushed forward by the inhomogeneous product kernel P_{1:t}.
Recursive update of the marginal distribution: mu_t is obtained by integrating the kernel P_t against mu_{t-1}.
Action of the Markov kernel on scalar functions: P_t f(x) is the expected value of f under the one-step transition from x.
Extension of the Markov kernel action to matrix-valued functions, applied entrywise.
Definition of the Euclidean norm of a complex vector.
Definition of the operator norm of a matrix as the supremum of ||Ax||/||x|| over nonzero x.
Definition of the Frobenius norm of a matrix via the trace of A^* A.
Definition of the uniform norm ||F||_infty of a matrix-valued function as the supremum of operator norms.
Matrix Laplace-transform bound: the tail probability of the largest eigenvalue is controlled by the trace of the matrix moment generating function.
GLSS multi-matrix Golden-Thompson inequality: the trace-exponential of a sum of Hermitian matrices is bounded by an averaged trace of ordered matrix-exponential products.
Definition of the twisted matrix exponentials W_t(x) and their adjoints used in the GLSS reduction.
equation: W_t(x):=\exp\!\Big(\frac12 e^{i\phi}\,s\,\widetilde F_t(x)\Big), \qquad W_t(x)^\ast=\exp\!\Big(\frac12 e^{-i\phi}\,s\,\widetilde F_t(x)\Big),

claim: Definition of the centered observables tilde-F_t = F_t - mu_t(F_t).
Definition of the ordered product M_j of twisted exponentials along the chain trajectory.
Definition of a_j(phi) as the expected trace of M_j M_j^*, the key mgf-related quantity.
Renewal construction: recursive definitions of the matrices Theta_{n,i}, their expectations B_{n,i}, and the centered remainders H_{n,i}.
Definition of the renewal coefficients b_{n,i}(phi) as operator norms of the B_{n,i} matrices.
Renewal inequality: the mgf quantity a_n(phi) is bounded by a convolution of the coefficients b_{n,i} with the earlier values a_{n-i}.
Coefficient-sum condition: if the b_{n,i} sum to at most 1 + C s^2, the mgf grows at most exponentially in n.
Generic mgf bound: under the coefficient-sum condition, the matrix mgf is bounded by m^{2-pi/4} exp(C n s^2).
Identity linking the twisted exponentials: W_n^* W_n collapses to the renewal term Theta_{n,1}.
equation: W_n(X_n)^\ast W_n(X_n) = \exp\!\Big(\frac12 e^{-i\phi}\,s\,\widetilde F_n(X_n)\Big) \exp\!\Big(\frac12 e^{i\phi}\,s\,\widetilde F_n(X_n)\Big) = \exp\!\Big( \gamma\,s\,\widetilde F_n(X_n)\Big) = \Theta_{n,1}(X_n).

claim: Renewal decomposition identity: a_n(phi) splits into a sum of B_{n,i} terms plus a vanishing centered remainder.
GLSS reduction: the matrix moment generating function is bounded by m^{1-pi/4} times the supremum of a_n(phi) over the twist angle.
equation: \E_{\mu_0}\tr\exp\!\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{4} s\sum_{j=1}^n \widetilde F_j(X_j)\Bigr) \le m^{1-\pi/4}\sup_{\phi\in[-\pi/2,\pi/2]} \E\tr(M_n M_n^\ast) = m^{1-\pi/4}\sup_{\phi\in[-\pi/2,\pi/2]} a_n(\phi).

claim: Scalar Lipschitz-contraction hypothesis: the Markov operator contracts scalar Lipschitz constants by a factor a.
Scalar-to-matrix Lipschitz lift: scalar Lipschitz contractivity of P implies the same contraction for Hermitian matrix-valued functions in operator norm.
Variational characterization of the operator norm of (PF)(x)-(PF)(y) as a supremum of quadratic forms over unit vectors.
Centering identity: a centered function equals the integral of its increments against its centering measure.
Diameter-centering lemma: a centered Lipschitz matrix function has sup norm at most D times its operator Lipschitz constant.
Bounds on the twisted exponentials W_j: uniform-norm and operator-Lipschitz bounds in terms of s, L, and D.
Coefficient bounds for the curvature regime: b_{n,1} is near 1, and later coefficients carry curvature-discounted contraction products.
Three-term decomposition of B_{n,i} after centering the twisted exponentials around their means.
equation: B_{n,i} =\mu_\tau\!\big((W_\tau-\mu_\tau W_\tau)\,G\,(\mu_\tau W_\tau)^\ast\big) +\mu_\tau\!\big((\mu_\tau W_\tau)\,G\,(W_\tau^\ast-\mu_\tau W_\tau^\ast)\big) +\mu_\tau\!\big((W_\tau-\mu_\tau W_\tau)\,G\,(W_\tau^\ast-\mu_\tau W_\tau^\ast)\big).

claim: Refined prefactor bound on the operator norm of B_{n,i} in terms of s, L, D and the mean of ||G||.
Tilted renewal lemma: even with an exponential tilt of e^{pi kappa/24} per factor, the curvature-discounted products sum to at most 3/kappa.
Definitions of the auxiliary sums a_t and b_t used in the tilted-renewal induction.
Recurrences for the auxiliary sums: a_t = u_t(1 + a_{t-1}) and b_t = 1 + r u_t b_{t-1}.
Summed coefficient bound: the b_{n,i} sum to at most 1 + 6 s^2 L^2 D^2 kappa^{-1} after absorbing the exponential tilt.
Matrix mgf bound in the curvature regime with variance proxy v^2 = 192 L^2 D^2/(pi^2 kappa).
equation: \E_{\mu_0}\tr\exp\!\Bigl(r\sum_{j=1}^n \widetilde F_j(X_j)\Bigr) \le m^{2-\pi/4}\exp\!\Bigl(\frac{16C}{\pi^2}n r^2\Bigr) = m^{2-\pi/4}\exp\!\Bigl(\frac12 n v^2 r^2\Bigr),

claim: Per-term deviation bound: each centered observable is bounded in operator norm by LD.
Homogeneous curvature hypothesis for the asymptotic-variance illustration: the kernel contracts W1 by (1-kappa).
Regularity conditions for the scalar asymptotic-variance bound: f is L-Lipschitz with oscillation at most Delta <= LD.
Asymptotic variance bound: sigma^2_as(f) <= C Delta^2 kappa^{-1} (1 + log(LD/Delta)) for a stationary positively-curved chain.
Stationary covariance decomposition of the normalized variance of a sum into the variance plus weighted lag covariances.
Covariance identity: the lag-i covariance equals the integral of f against P^i f under stationarity.
Oscillation bound on the sup norm of P^i f for a centered f.
Iterated Lipschitz contraction: Lip(P^i f) decays geometrically as L(1-kappa)^i.
Combined sup-norm profile for P^i f taking the minimum of the oscillation bound and the Lipschitz-contraction bound.
Lag-covariance bound with the min-profile; the key estimate behind the logarithmic variance proxy.
Definition of the crossover lag i_star where the Lipschitz-contraction bound overtakes the oscillation bound.
Summed min-profile bound: the covariance profile sums to at most 2 + kappa^{-1} log(LD/Delta) + kappa^{-1}.
Finite-n variance bound with the logarithmic variance proxy 7 Delta^2 kappa^{-1} (1 + log(LD/Delta)).
Definition: an increasing concave function psi controls the increments of a matrix-valued function H.
Concave-profile contraction lemma: a positively curved operator improves an increment profile psi to psi((1-kappa) .).
Optimal-coupling identity: the expected coupled distance equals the W1 distance, bounded by (1-kappa)d(x,y) under curvature.
Base increment profile psi_1 for the renewal remainders, combining the oscillation and Lipschitz scales.
Recursive definition of the scale profiles psi_j controlling the increments of the renewal remainders H_{n,j}.
Centered-observable sup bound: the operator norm of tilde-F_t(x) is at most Delta_op.
Increment bound for centered observables via the oscillation scale: Delta_op times min{1, L d/Delta_op}.
Increment bound for the first renewal remainder H_{n,1}.
Sharp window-sum lemma: the renewal coefficients sum to at most 1 + 100 s^2 Delta_op^2 kappa^{-1} (1 + log(LD/Delta_op)).
Definition of the evaluated profiles q_{j,k} = psi_j((1-kappa)^k D).
Recurrence for the evaluated profiles q_{j,k}.
Renewal equation for q_{j,1} expressing it through earlier profile values and the min-profile weights.
Definition of the auxiliary sum S weighting the min-profile by the exponential tilt.
Exponential majorization of the min-profile using 1-kappa <= e^{-kappa}.
Bound on the auxiliary sum: S <= 10 (1 + log(LD/Delta_op))/kappa.
Summed profile bound: the sum of q_{j,1} over j is at most 20 s Delta_op (1 + log(LD/Delta_op))/kappa.
Bound on the first renewal coefficient: b_{n,1}(phi) <= exp(s^2 Delta_op^2/2) <= 1 + s^2 Delta_op^2.
Per-coefficient bound: b_{n,i}(phi) <= 2 s Delta_op e^{s Delta_op} q_{i-1,1} for i >= 2.
Summed tail bound for the renewal coefficients with i >= 2.
Definition of the admissible mgf range rbar_max for the diameter-improved Chernoff bound.
Matrix mgf bound in the diameter-improved regime with variance proxy vbar^2.
Tightness example: the dyadic Bernoulli chain X_{t+1} = X_t/2 + (D/2) B_{t+1} with i.i.d. fair Bernoulli bits.
The dyadic chain contracts W1 by 1/2 per step, hence has Ollivier curvature at least 1/2.
Definition of the frequency cutoff ell as the largest integer with pi Delta 2^ell <= LD.
Definition of the tightness-example observables F_t(x) = (Delta/2) cos(2 pi 2^t x/D).
Lipschitz bound for the tightness observables, verified through the frequency cutoff.
Initial distribution of the tightness example: uniform on [0,D], which is the chain's stationary law.
Unrolled closed form of the dyadic chain as a scaled initial value plus a dyadic Bernoulli sum.
Dyadic identity: 2^t X_t/D equals X_0/D plus an integer.
Collapse identity: each observable F_t(X_t) depends only on the starting point X_0.
Definition of the centered partial sum S_ell for the tightness example.
Closed form of the partial sum: S_ell = (Delta/2) ell cos(2 pi X_0/D).
Hypothetical sub-Gaussian tail form used to derive the variance lower bound.
Exact lower-bound probability: P(S_ell > Delta ell/4) = 1/3 from the uniform law of X_0.
Implied variance lower bound: any valid variance proxy v^2 must satisfy v^2 >= ell epsilon^2/(2 log 3).
Matching lower bound: v^2 = Omega(Delta^2 kappa^{-1} log(LD/Delta)), proving the logarithmic variance proxy is tight up to constants.
L2 contraction computation: P_t is non-expansive from L^2(mu_t) to L^2(mu_{t-1}) by Jensen's inequality and the marginal recursion.
Definition of the matrix L^2(nu) norm via the Frobenius norm: ||F||_{2,nu}^2 = integral of ||F||_F^2.
Spectral lift lemma: the one-step singular value sigma_t contracts centered Hermitian matrix functions in the matrix L^2 norm.
Frobenius decomposition of the matrix L^2 norm into a sum of scalar L^2 norms of the matrix entries.
Entrywise L^2 contraction: each scalar entry of P_t F contracts by sigma_t.
Spectral-regime bounds on the twisted exponentials W_t in terms of the oscillation Delta_op.
equation: \|W_t(x)\|_{\op}\le e^{\frac12 s\Delta_{\op}}, \qquad \sup_{x,y \in \Omega} \|W_t(x)-W_t(y)\|_{\op} \le \tfrac12 s\Delta_{\op}\, e^{\frac12 s\Delta_{\op}}, \qquad \|H_{n,1}\|_{\infty}\le s\Delta_{\op}\, e^{s\Delta_{\op}}.

claim: Spectral coefficient bounds: b_{n,i} controlled by s^2 Delta_op Delta_F times tilted singular-value products.
Norm comparison: the centered sup norm is bounded by Delta_op, which is at most the Frobenius oscillation Delta_F.
Spectral prefactor bound on the operator norm of B_{n,i} in terms of s, Delta_op and the mean of ||G||.
Operator-to-Frobenius reduction: mu_tau(||G||_op) is bounded by the matrix L^2 norm of G.
L^2 contraction of the renewal remainder: the L^2 norm of P_{tau+1} H_{n,i-1} is controlled by sigma_{tau+1}.
Recursive L^2 bound for the renewal remainders H_{n,i} with tilted singular values.
Sup-Frobenius bound for the Theta_1 increments in terms of s, Delta_op, and Delta_F.
equation: \sup_{x,y}\|\Theta_1(x)-\Theta_1(y)\|_{\mathrm F} \le e^{\|\gamma s\widetilde F_n\|_{\infty}}\cdot |\gamma|s\cdot \sup_{x,y}\|\widetilde F_n(x)-\widetilde F_n(y)\|_{\mathrm F} \le s e^{s\Delta_{\op}}\Delta_{\mathrm F}.

claim: L^2 bound on the first renewal remainder: ||H_{n,1}||_{2,mu_n} <= (s/sqrt(2)) e^{s Delta_op} Delta_F.
Definition of the spectral-regime constant C = 24 Delta_op Delta_F / lambda.
Matrix mgf bound in the spectral regime with constant C.
Definition of the spectral variance proxy v_B^2 = 768 Delta_op Delta_F/(pi^2 lambda).
Combined Bernstein-type bound for the spectral regime: the minimum of the sub-Gaussian and boundary-optimized exponents.
equation: \Pbb_{\mu_0}\Big(\lambda_{\max}\Big(\sum_{j=1}^n \widetilde F_j(X_j)\Big)\ge n\varepsilon\Big) \le m^{2-\pi/4}\, \exp\Big(-n\cdot \min\Big\{\frac{\varepsilon^2}{2v_B^2},\; r_{\max}\varepsilon-\tfrac12 v_B^2 r_{\max}^2\Big\}\Big),

claim: Definitions of the admissible range r_max and the constant C for the spectral Chernoff proof.
Summed coefficient bound in the spectral regime: the b_{n,i} sum to at most 1 + C s^2.
equation: \sum_{i=1}^n b_{n,i}(\phi) &\le e^{2s^2\Delta_{\op}\Delta_{\mathrm F}} +4s^2\Delta_{\op}\Delta_{\mathrm F}e^{2s\Delta_{\op}} \sum_{i=2}^n \prod_{\ell=n-i+2}^{n}(e^{s\Delta_{\op}}\sigma_\ell) \\ &\le 1+8s^2\Delta_{\op}\Delta_{\mathrm F} \sum_{i=1}^n \prod_{\ell=n-i+2}^{n}(e^{\lambda/8}\sigma_\ell) \\ &\le 1+C s^2.

claim: Rank-based comparison: Delta_F <= sqrt(2 sup rank F_t) Delta_op, so the two oscillations are comparable for low-rank observables.
Definition of L^2_0(nu) as the zero-mean subspace of L^2(nu).
Definition of the one-step second singular value sigma_t as the operator norm of P_t on zero-mean L^2 functions.
Scalar L^2 contraction: ||P_t f||_{2,mu_{t-1}} <= sigma_t ||f||_{2,mu_t} for zero-mean f.
Spectral Chernoff theorem: matrix concentration with variance proxy v_B^2 under a positive spectral gap, requiring neither bounded diameter nor Lipschitz observables.
Hermitian Hoeffding lemma: the matrix mgf of a bounded centered Hermitian random matrix is dominated by exp(s^2 R^2/2) times the identity.
Matrix exponential difference bound in operator norm.
Matrix exponential difference bound in Frobenius norm.
Integral representation of the difference of two matrix exponentials.
Lipschitz product rule for matrix-valued functions in operator norm.
